commands.run: (until curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:5080/sensors/boiler/readings; do sleep 1; done; for s in 25:18.5 15:20.0 5:21.5; do curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5080/readings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"sensor\":\"boiler\",\"at\":\"$(date -u -d "-${s%%:*} minutes" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\",\"celsius\":${s##*:}}" >/dev/null; done) & exec dotnet run --project src/Readings/Readings.csproj --no-build
commands.seed: for s in 25:18.5 15:20.0 5:21.5; do curl -sS -X POST "$ASPNETCORE_URLS/readings" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"sensor\":\"boiler\",\"at\":\"$(date -u -d "-${s%%:*} minutes" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\",\"celsius\":${s##*:}}"; echo; done

env.name: ASPNETCORE_URLS
env.why: The address Kestrel binds. src/Readings/Program.cs calls WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args) and there is no Properties/launchSettings.json, so without this the host falls back to its built-in default (:5000) and nothing would be listening where app_url points. This is the app's own real origin inside the sandbox, not a placeholder.

env.name: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT
env.why: Selects the host environment. Development keeps the developer exception page and per-request logging on, so a verifier reading the run log sees which endpoint failed and why instead of a bare 500. No code branches on it; the host does.

env.name: DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT
env.why: The .NET SDK's first run posts usage telemetry. The sandbox should not make a network call the repo never asked for.

env.name: DOTNET_NOLOGO
env.why: Suppresses the SDK first-run banner so the tail of a failing build is the failure rather than the welcome message.

dropped.why: That step provisions an SDK on a bare runner; it is CI plumbing, not something the app needs installed. The trial runner already ships .NET SDKs, and a newer SDK builds this repo's net9.0 target fine — verified here against SDK 11.0.100, which produced 0 warnings with TreatWarningsAsErrors on.

It is a lint gate, not a build or a test. `bsf gates static` runs the repo's own linters, and folding it into `test` would make a whitespace nit report as a failing test. It is recorded in the runbook and it passes here.

dropped.what: The bare `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` forms, without --no-restore / --no-build
dropped.why: Kept the staged forms instead so install, build and test are three separable steps the trial can attribute a failure to; the README's forms re-restore and re-build on every invocation.

exercised: dotnet restore and dotnet build with TreatWarningsAsErrors, EnforceCodeStyleInBuild and AnalysisLevel=latest-recommended, so any analyzer or code-style warning fails the build rather than scrolling past
the six xUnit tests in tests/Readings.Tests/ReadingStoreTests.cs, covering every public member of ReadingStore (TryAdd, For, MeanCelsius)
the two decisions the repo says matter: MeanCelsius returning null and not 0 for an empty window, and TryAdd refusing a -127C reading instead of storing it

the HTTP surface in src/Readings/Program.cs end to end against a running app: POST /readings (202 accepted, 400 with the range message for -127), GET /sensors/{sensor}/readings (200, newest first), GET /sensors/{sensor}/mean (200 with the mean, 204 for an empty window, 400 when ?minutes is absent)
a browser screenshot of GET /sensors/boiler/readings after the run command seeds three readings, so a change to the JSON shape is visible and not only asserted

not_exercised.what: Anything that survives a restart. ReadingStore is a ConcurrentDictionary in process memory and the repo has no database, file store or migration, so state in the sandbox lasts exactly as long as the run command.
not_exercised.why: There is nothing to persist to. A change that introduced a store needs an amendment adding that service to the sandbox; nothing here would catch a persistence bug.

not_exercised.what: Concurrent writes. TryAdd takes a lock on the per-sensor list and the dictionary is concurrent, but no test and no trial step issues two overlapping requests.
not_exercised.why: Every test constructs its own store on one thread and the trial drives the API one curl at a time. A race in the lock or sort would pass everything here.

not_exercised.what: The HTTP layer under `dotnet test`. Program.cs is declared `public partial class Program` specifically so a test project could host it, but tests/Readings.Tests references neither Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing nor WebApplicationFactory, so routing, model binding and JSON serialisation have no automated test.
not_exercised.why: The trial reaches these paths over real HTTP and the screenshot shows the serialised shape, but a regression in them fails no test, so the test gate alone will not catch it.

not_exercised.what: Coverage measurement. No coverage collector is configured in either csproj, and .factory/guardrails/coverage.json has high_pct and floor_pct at 0.
not_exercised.why: `dotnet test` emits no coverage data here, so the coverage half of gate 2 has nothing to read. Turning it on needs a collector package added to the test project.
None are configured anywhere in the repo. ASPNETCORE_URLS is http on loopback, so there is no TLS path and no identity to assert against.

Re-ran every later command with it unset, and under `env -i` with exactly the trial's six base variables, to be sure the fix was the environment and not a lucky inherit.

episode.observed: Listening on 127.0.0.1:5080. POST /readings 202; POST with celsius -127 returns 400 and {"error":"-127C is outside the plausible range"}; GET /sensors/boiler/readings returns the list newest first; GET /sensors/boiler/mean?minutes=60 returns the mean; the same for an unknown sensor returns 204; omitting ?minutes returns 400. episode.tried: Put a readiness loop and three seeding POSTs in front of the server in the run command, then opened the app in Chromium through playwright-cli and took a full-page screenshot — the same thing the trial does with `npx playwright screenshot`.
episode.observed: The page shows the three seeded readings as JSON, newest first, each with its timestamp and celsius. The seeder runs in a background subshell and the server is `exec`ed, so the process the trial spawns is the server itself and its SIGTERM to the process group reaches both. If the seeding ever fails the page still returns 200 with [], so a broken seed costs the data in the screenshot, not the tier.
